install.title: Install Canary
install.description: Add Canary from your node platform marketplace, or follow the source-available manual setup. Use Canary Cloud if you are not installing on a node.

wallet.title: Add watch-only wallet information
wallet.description: Provide a descriptor, XPUB, or individual Bitcoin address. Single-sig and multisig wallets are both supported. Never enter a seed phrase or private key.

notifications.title: Choose notifications
notifications.description: Configure ntfy, Nostr, or webhooks and decide where alerts should be delivered.

languages.title: Multilingual notifications
languages.description: Receive alert content in any of Canary’s supported languages.

privacy.title: Privacy is more than private keys
privacy.description: Self hosting reduces what you share with Canary, but every notification route has its own exposure.

walletData.title: Wallet data privacy
walletData.description: When self hosted, Canary stores descriptors, XPUBs, addresses, balances, and transaction history on infrastructure you control. A configured notification can still send selected event details to its delivery service.

spendingKeys.title: Spending key safety
spendingKeys.description: Canary never needs private keys or seed phrases and cannot authorize a Bitcoin transaction.

notifications.title: Notification privacy varies
notifications.description: Notification services can learn connection metadata and, depending on configuration, message content. ntfy servers, Nostr relays, and webhook operators each see different information.

cloud.title: Do not have a node, or prefer not to run Canary yourself?
cloud.description: Canary Cloud runs the same watch-only monitoring for you, with email and SMS alerts that are not available when you self-host.

operation.question: Where does Canary run?
operation.answer: The self-hosted edition runs on your Bitcoin node or server and connects to the Bitcoin infrastructure configured by that deployment.

privateKeys.question: Does Canary need my private keys?
privateKeys.answer: No. Canary uses descriptors, XPUBs, or addresses for watch-only monitoring of single-sig and multisig wallets. It cannot sign transactions or spend funds.

nodes.question: Which node platforms are supported?
nodes.answer: Production packages are available for Umbrel, Start9, and the myNode Marketplace. GitHub contains source and manual setup information.

methods.question: How can Canary notify me?
methods.answer: Self-hosted Canary supports ntfy, Nostr, and webhooks. Canary Cloud adds email and SMS, which are not available when you self-host, and also supports ntfy.

privacy.question: Are notifications completely private?
privacy.answer: No notification channel is automatically private. ntfy servers, Nostr relays, and webhook operators expose different connection metadata and may receive message content depending on your configuration.

cloud.question: How is Canary Cloud different?
cloud.answer: Cloud is a hosted paid service for people who do not have a node or do not want to run Canary themselves. It includes email and SMS alerts, stores the watch-only wallet data you provide, and can connect it to account and billing identity, but it never receives private keys and cannot spend funds.

faq.title: Privacy questions
faq.description: Hosted monitoring needs watch-only wallet data to do its job. These are the important details.

walletData.question: What wallet data does Canary Cloud store?
walletData.answer: Canary Cloud stores the descriptors, XPUBs, or addresses you supply, including single-sig and multisig wallets.

visibility.question: Can Canary Cloud see wallet activity?
visibility.answer: Yes. That watch-only information can reveal wallet addresses, balances, and transaction history.

identity.question: Is wallet data linked to my account?
identity.answer: Your Canary account and subscription can connect wallet information to your account and billing identity.

privateKeys.question: Does Canary Cloud get my private keys?
